clue.text: Some of these Dickensians turned up for a day in 24 down reportedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the run is read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of these two words are taken, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: A few of the people in Dickens's novels have been turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' picks SEDI from theSE DIckensians, and 'turned up' reads it upwards. 24 down is ROAM, which sounds like Rome, hence 'reportedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides was the middle day of certain months, famously the fifteenth of March.

clue.text: Hit written after 22 down half cut grass

indicators.note: the strike word is placed after the halved surname
cutting the word in half keeps only its first three letters

parts.note: 22 down's answer is the surname from Dickens's ghost
to ram is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A blow recorded after a drunken grass-cutting session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' suggests drunk, but here it halves the surname; 'written after' puts the strike word behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass planted on sand dunes to bind them.

clue.text: Irate Welsh dancing group — were they …

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Angry Welsh people dance in a troupe, and a question follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges IRATE WELSH. The trailing 'were they …' leads into the next clue: a band called the Wailers might be crying.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wailers were Bob Marley's reggae band, a musical group.

clue.text: … caught being 25 after piano disappeared?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the musical letter has gone from the word, leaving what follows
the musical letter has gone from the word, leaving what follows

parts.note: 25 down is NOSY, and being nosy is prying
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone caught snooping once the piano went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the previous clue: 'were they …' (the Wailers) doing this. 'after piano disappeared' drops P from the nosy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wailers by name would be expected to be weeping, which is what the linked question implies.

clue.text: Magazine once distributed in Paris — and Bern briefly

indicators.note: distributed spreads the letters out into a new arrangement
briefly cuts the last letter from the city name

explanation.surface: A periodical that used to be circulated in Paris and, for a short time, Bern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' turns BERN into BER; 'distributed' rearranges PARIS plus BER.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare Rib was a British feminist magazine published from 1972 to 1993.

clue.text: Adult taken in by party game

indicators.note: the party's letters take in, or contain, the adult's letter

parts.note: SNP is the Scottish National Party
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up is fooled at a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' suggests deceived, but means contained: A inside SNP.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a children's card game where matching cards are called out.

clue.text: Position of a small singer in performing duet

indicators.note: performing works the letters into a different arrangement

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Where a little vocalist stands while singing a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small singer' suggests a child vocalist, but it is the bird; 'performing' rearranges bird and DUET together.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude can be a bodily posture or stance, a sense of position.

clue.text: Hue and cry about doctor getting struck off

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are shuffled round

explanation.surface: An outcry concerning a doctor being removed from the medical register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hue and cry' looks like one phrase, but 'Hue' is the definition. Rearrange AND CRY with DR 'getting struck off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, so it is a hue.

clue.text: Hated going round a bit back in unroadworthy car?

indicators.note: going round turns the letters about into a new order
back means this word for a bit is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: Someone hated driving around in an old banger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges HATED; 'back' turns the bit round. 'car?' marks the definition as a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is anything dangerous enough to kill, as a dangerously unsafe vehicle may be.

clue.text: Spruce tree's first seen in Bath, not the outskirts in another city

indicators.note: these letters go inside the abbreviation for the other city

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: dropping the outskirts of the city name keeps only its centre
the first letter of the tree word is the one seen

explanation.surface: A spruce is seen in Bath, but not in the outskirts, and in another city too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree but is the adjective. AT from Bath plus T go 'in' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smartly dressed and neat, which is what spruce means as an adjective.

clue.text: Scolding woman was heartless with her rollicking

indicators.note: rollicking signals the letters are tumbled into a new order
heartless removes the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nagging wife was cold-hearted while telling her off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' makes WS from WAS; 'rollicking' rearranges WS and HER. A rollicking is also British slang for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging woman, as in The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: UN priority involved no unknown breaking in

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: The United Nations' main concern involved no unknown burglaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no unknown' removes Y from UN PRIORITY; 'involved' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An irruption is a sudden forcible entry, a bursting in.

clue.text: Flipping major road's no good for getting stuck

indicators.note: flipping turns the abbreviation over so it reads backwards

parts.note: MAJ is the abbreviation for the army rank of major
the M1 is a British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: An exasperated driver complains that the main road is useless for traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swearword but reverses MAJ to JAM. The M1 is England's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamming means becoming wedged so as to stop moving, being stuck.

clue.text: Dickensian nut that's spread out on grass topless

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second
the spread is opened out to wrap round the nut

parts.note: jam is a spread
a cob is a hazelnut

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter

parts.note: barley is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is a nutcase lying on the grass without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The spread is laid 'out' around the nut, giving JACOBM; 'topless' drops the first letter of the cereal. The theme swaps Jacob Marley and Bob Cratchit into Bob Marley.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Marley is Scrooge's dead partner in A Christmas Carol by Dickens.

clue.text: Tail of diver or another bird, not one that's a big swimmer

indicators.note: the tail of the word is its final letter
not removes the letter for one from the bird

parts.note: a quail is a game bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The tail of a diving bird or another bird, unlike one large creature in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail of' gives R; 'not one' takes I from QUAIL. Diver is a bird, so solvers look for a bird answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rorqual is a baleen whale such as the blue whale, a huge swimmer.

clue.text: Dire tempo applied to end of McEwan's Atonement

indicators.note: applied means put to work, so the letters are used in a new order
end of takes the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A bad pace marred the conclusion of Ian McEwan's novel Atonement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' rearranges DIRE TEMPO; 'end of' takes N from McEwan. Atonement looks like the novel's title but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Redemption is atonement, making amends for sin; Redemption Song is also a Bob Marley track.

clue.text: Places to swim for the larger figured person when topless?

parts.note: the clue describes the answer once its top, a lid, is gone, so that top is the opening piece
OS stands for outsize, the clothing size for a larger figure

explanation.surface: Bathing spots for big people who sunbathe without tops?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'topless' literally: remove the lid from the answer and OS, outsize, is what is left for the larger person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lidos are open-air public swimming pools.

clue.text: One church infiltrating another's hiding place

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside the other church

parts.note: CE, the Church of England, is another church
A means one

explanation.surface: One church sneaks into a rival's secret hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is another church, the Church of England; A, 'One', joins CH inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or weapons, or the hiding place itself.

clue.text: See 19 across
Dickensian advice for treating itch, involving shilling in change?

indicators.note: the shilling abbreviation S is changed for its slang name

parts.note: the natural advice for an itch is to scratch it
a bob was British slang for a shilling

explanation.surface: A Dickensian remedy for an itch, involving a shilling in loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the old abbreviation for a shilling (pre-1971 British coin, slang 'bob'); 'in change' swaps that S for BOB. 'Change' looks like coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's underpaid clerk in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.

clue.text: Mad about daughter getting the sack over things never getting settled

indicators.note: the mad word goes about the other pieces

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

indicators.note: over turns the word back to front

parts.note: bed is the sack, as in hitting the sack

explanation.surface: Someone is angry that their daughter went to bed with debts still outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the sack' looks like being fired, but the sack is bed, turned 'over' to give DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad debts are sums owed that will never be paid.

clue.text: Old man holding army corps in awe

indicators.note: holding means the father word contains the corps

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A father in the army corps is held in respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is father, not an old soldier, despite the army context. Dread is also a nod to Rastafarian dreadlocks and Marley.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, and awe is fearful reverence.

clue.text: Cooked with a little brown bread, say

indicators.note: a little of the colour word means just its first letter

parts.note: bread made with yeast is raised bread, so 'say' gives an example of something raised

explanation.surface: Prepared with a small amount of wholemeal loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes B from brown, then RAISED, describing leavened bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a covered pot with little liquid.

clue.text: Artists masquerading as people hesitating to follow my lead

indicators.note: the hesitating people come after the first letter
the lead of the word is its first letter

parts.note: people who say um when unsure are ummers

explanation.surface: Performers in disguise are reluctant people following my example.
explanation.walkthrough: M is 'my lead'; UMMERS 'to follow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummers are actors in traditional masked folk plays.

clue.text: See 13
Used mobile outside times to ring if going out …

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the other pieces
mobile means moving, so the letters move about

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign for times
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A secondhand mobile phone is used abroad to make calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges USED, which goes 'outside' X and O. The clue runs on into 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, a going out.

clue.text: Teller of tales has crane cavorting with lots of …

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order
lots of a word is most of it, all but its last letter

parts.note: the dots point to the answer of the next clue, the fish

explanation.surface: A storyteller has a crane prancing with a crowd of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots stand for the next answer, TROUT; 'lots of' gives TROU, and 'cavorting' rearranges CRANE plus TROU.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells anecdotes skilfully.

clue.text: … to use it abroad, say, with nothing in memory

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the memory word

parts.note: RAM is computer memory
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Using a phone overseas with no storage left.
explanation.walkthrough: O inside RAM. It continues 23 down: roaming is using a mobile abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaming is using a mobile phone on a foreign network, a typical example of using one abroad.

clue.text: Inquisitive new sailor sat on top of yardarm

indicators.note: in a down clue the sailor is placed above the next letter

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: the top of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A curious new sailor perched at the top of the yardarm.
explanation.walkthrough: N and OS sit on Y, the 'top of' yardarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy means prying, too curious about others.

clue.text: … fish from the River Ouse, until tickling starts

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Fish from the Yorkshire Ouse, until someone starts to tickle them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes initials of The River Ouse Until Tickling. Tickling is a real way to catch trout by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: One of 3 originally displayed in Photoshop

indicators.note: the letters are on display within the software name

explanation.surface: A band member's picture appears in edited software.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is THE WAILERS: Peter Tosh was one of the original members.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Tosh was a founding member of the Wailers with Bob Marley.

clue.text: Sign tooth decay hasn't started, as seen in the mirror at 2?

indicators.note: the opening letter is missing

parts.note: caries is the dental term for tooth decay

explanation.surface: A star sign seen in the bathroom mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as seen in the mirror at 2?' is a nod to 2 down: MARRAM holds RAM, Aries' symbol, and its mirror image MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Leader of Uriah Heep's got to reform group

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new order
the leader of the name is its first letter

parts.note: the name with its 's supplies the letter S

explanation.surface: The head of Dickens's Uriah Heep must reform his gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' gives U; 'to reform' rearranges U, HEEPS and GOT. Uriah Heep is a Dickens villain and a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pogues were an Anglo-Irish folk-punk band, a musical group.
